sources.notes: Seven authentic letters written en route to martyrdom. Earliest evidence of episcopal church structure.
sources.citation_info: Letter to the Ephesians, Letter to the Romans, Letter to the Smyrnaeans. See especially Romans 4:1: 'I am the wheat of God'

sources.notes: Governor's correspondence with Emperor Trajan about Christians. Describes early Christian worship practices.
sources.citation_info: Book 10, Letter 96: Correspondence with Emperor Trajan asking how to handle Christians in Bithynia. Describes Christians meeting before dawn, singing hymns to Christ 'as to a god'

sources.work: First Apology and Dialogue with Trypho
sources.notes: Philosophical defense of Christianity to Roman authorities. Describes baptism and Eucharist practices.
sources.citation_info: First Apology, Chapters 61-67: Detailed description of Christian worship, baptism, and Eucharist. Dialogue with Trypho: Jewish-Christian debate

sources.notes: Systematic refutation of Gnosticism. Establishes four-gospel canon and apostolic succession.
sources.citation_info: Book 3, Chapter 3, Section 2: Famous passage on apostolic succession and Roman church. Book 3, Chapter 11: Defense of four gospels as divinely ordained number

sources.notes: Brilliant Latin apologist, coined term 'Trinity.' Later joined Montanist movement.
sources.citation_info: Apologeticum, Chapter 39: 'See how these Christians love one another.' De Spectaculis: Against pagan entertainment

sources.notes: Earliest Christian martyrdom account outside New Testament. Letter from Smyrna church.
sources.citation_info: Chapters 9-15: Account of Polycarp's arrest, trial, and death by burning. Chapter 9: 'Eighty-six years I have served Him'

sources.notes: Gnostic gospel containing 114 sayings of Jesus. Discovered at Nag Hammadi 1945.
sources.citation_info: Saying 1: 'Whoever finds the interpretation of these sayings will not experience death.' Sayings 13-14, 77, 114

sources.notes: Early church manual on ethics, rituals, and church organization. Nearly made it into NT canon.
sources.citation_info: Chapters 7-10: Instructions on baptism, fasting, and Eucharist. Chapters 11-13: On traveling prophets and apostles

sources.notes: Apocalyptic work popular in early church. Contains visions, mandates, and parables.
sources.citation_info: Vision 3: The church as an old woman. Mandate 4: On repentance. Widely read, considered scriptural by some churches

sources.work: Lost Christianities: The Battles for Scripture and the Faiths We Never Knew
sources.notes: Examines diversity of early Christianity and texts excluded from canon.
sources.citation_info: Chapter 1: 'The Ancient Discovery of a Forgery.' Chapters 4-6: On Gnostic texts, Ebionites, and Marcionites

sources.work: Orthodoxy and Heresy in Earliest Christianity
sources.notes: Revolutionary thesis that 'heresy' often preceded 'orthodoxy' in many regions.
sources.citation_info: Chapter 1: 'Edessa.' Chapter 2: 'Egypt.' Challenged traditional narrative of unified early orthodoxy

sources.work: Augustus to Constantine: The Rise and Triumph of Christianity in the Roman World
sources.notes: Classic study of Christianity's growth in Roman Empire through Constantine.
sources.citation_info: Chapters 5-8: On 2nd century development, martyrdoms, and apologetics

sources.work: Martyrdom and Persecution in the Early Church
sources.notes: Comprehensive study of persecution from Jesus to Constantine.
sources.citation_info: Part 2, Chapters 6-12: Detailed analysis of 2nd century persecutions under Trajan, Marcus Aurelius, and Severus
